proof_summary: The relevant difference is rewritten using \(\beta(S,N)=[X^N]\,\frac{1-2X}{(1-X)(1-X+X^2)}(1-X)^{-S}\), and a Dwork–Cartier expansion based on \(\Delta=X^p+(1-X)^p=1+ph\) and \(h=(1-X)(1-X+X^2)\eta\) yields a double-sum identity in which the low-order moments vanish by a Cartier fixed-point relation and the involution \(X\mapsto1-X\). Kummer–Legendre and Stirling-number valuation bounds, combined with a product identity for the remaining inner sums, show every term has \(p\)-adic valuation at least \(3(v+1)\) when \(p^v\mid S,N\); taking \(v=k-1\) gives the result.
